literature_notes: L1 and L2 report full-length DSC3-eGFP and DSC3-mCherry fusion constructs expressed in mammalian cells. The naming convention 'DSC3-eGFP' and 'DSC3-mCherry' denotes C-terminal fusions. DSC3 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein: its N-terminus is extracellular (mature residues 28–692) and its C-terminus is intracellular (712–896). A C-terminal fluorescent-protein fusion appended after residue 896 therefore resides in the cytoplasm, not on the extracellular face. This disqualifies L1/L2 from grounding any extracellular surface-tag site. L3 validates that DSC3 reaches the cell surface and supports EBV infection, but it reports protein function, not a tag position; it cannot pin an extracellular insertion site. No ledger line reports a tag, epitope, or any insertion on the extracellular domain of DSC3. Zero extracellular sites are supported.

literature_other_positions.note: DSC3-eGFP and DSC3-mCherry are C-terminal fusions; the DSC3 C-terminus (residues 712–896) is intracellular, so the fluorescent-protein tag is cytoplasmic, not on the extracellular surface.
